title: How to manage freight broker accessorial charge billing on Mac: a guide for brokers
metaTitle: Freight Broker Accessorial Charge Verification: A Guide for Mac Users
description: Learn how to handle freight broker accessorial charge billing, stop margin leaks, and use your Mac to automate the verification process.
intro: Managing a freight broker accessorial charge is a daily struggle that eats into your profit margins. You need to reconcile every extra fee against your original rate confirmation to ensure you are not overpaying for services that were never performed.
tldr: Accessorial charges like detention and lumper fees are major sources of margin loss.
Manual verification of these charges is slow and prone to human error.
Automating the reconciliation process saves time and prevents overpayments.

blocks.text: Why freight broker accessorial charge disputes happen

Accessorial charges are fees for services beyond the standard line-haul move. These include detention, lumper fees, stop-off charges, and layovers. The problem starts when these fees appear on a carrier invoice without prior documentation or approval. If you do not catch these discrepancies, they become a direct hit to your bottom line.

The primary cause is fragmented documentation. You have a rate confirmation, a bill of lading, a proof of delivery, and the final invoice. If the detention time on the invoice does not match the timestamp on the proof of delivery, you have a dispute. Many brokers rely on manual review, which is slow and inconsistent. When you are busy, it is tempting to approve smaller charges just to close the file. This leads to margin creep, where small overcharges accumulate into significant annual losses.
How to fix billing verification on your Mac

items: Standardize your rate confirmations to clearly define what counts as an accessorial charge.
Require drivers to submit signed proof of delivery documents with specific timestamps for detention.
Use a cloud-based TMS that allows you to upload documents directly from your Mac.
Run a quarterly audit of your carrier invoices against your contracts to find recurring errors.
Automate your data entry by using tools that read PDF invoices and compare them to your system data.

blocks.text: Remember that under 49 U.S. Code section 13710, you have a 180-day window to contest a freight bill. If you miss this window, you lose your right to dispute the charge.
blocks.title: Watch your deadlines

blocks.text: Using tools on your Mac for freight billing

Most modern freight brokerages use web-based tools. Since you are on a Mac, avoid legacy software that requires Windows virtualization. Tools like Tai TMS or Tailwind TMS run natively in Chrome or Safari. This allows you to manage your billing tasks without the performance issues common with older Windows-only applications.

faq.question: How do I spot an incorrect accessorial charge?
faq.answer: Compare the carrier invoice against your original rate confirmation and the signed proof of delivery. Look for discrepancies in detention time or extra fees that were not in the initial agreement.

faq.question: Can I automate this on a Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Use cloud-based TMS platforms that offer automated matching. These tools compare your invoice data against your system records automatically, flagging discrepancies for your review.
